components.css: .ds-ticket{position:relative;overflow:hidden;border-radius:22px;background:rgb(var(--c-card));border:1px solid var(--card-border);box-shadow:var(--shadow-card);color:rgb(var(--c-ink));font-family:Inter,sans-serif;animation:ds-print 520ms cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) both}.ds-ticket::before{content:'';position:absolute;width:60%;aspect-ratio:1;top:-30%;right:-12%;border-radius:50%;background:var(--glow-a);filter:blur(40px);pointer-events:none}.ds-t-head{position:relative;padding:20px 20px 12px}.ds-t-head strong{display:block;font-weight:700;font-size:17px;letter-spacing:-.01em}.ds-t-head span{font-size:13px;color:rgb(var(--c-muted))}.ds-t-tear{position:relative;height:22px;margin:0 -1px;background:radial-gradient(circle at 0 50%,rgb(var(--c-ground)) 10px,transparent 10.5px),radial-gradient(circle at 100% 50%,rgb(var(--c-ground)) 10px,transparent 10.5px)}.ds-t-tear::after{content:'';position:absolute;left:18px;right:18px;top:50%;border-top:1.5px dashed var(--line-strong)}.ds-t-stub{position:relative;display:flex;align-items:flex-end;gap:16px;padding:12px 20px 20px}.ds-t-stub p{margin:0 0 6px;font:600 13px/1 Inter,sans-serif;color:rgb(var(--c-muted))}.ds-t-total{font-size:38px;font-weight:900;line-height:1;letter-spacing:-.035em;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;margin-right:8px}.ds-t-fig{font-size:20px;font-weight:800;line-height:1;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;color:rgb(var(--c-muted))}.ds-t-left{color:rgb(var(--c-accent))}.ds-t-arrow{color:rgb(var(--c-faint));font-size:18px;line-height:1}@keyframes ds-print{from{opacity:0;transform:translateY(14px);filter:blur(6px)}to{opacity:1;transform:none;filter:none}}@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-ticket{animation:none}}

narrative.northStar: The Fitting Room After Closing Time
narrative.overview:
The shop is shut, the racks are quiet, and one mirror is still lit. Working screens are the calm part of the room: espresso surfaces, walnut cards stepped up in tone, linen text, and a single cognac accent for the one action that matters. Nothing glows, drifts or shimmers while you are describing what you need, choosing a budget or tidying a wardrobe. This is Palestra's locker-room structure, translated into brown.

The lit moment is the outfit. It arrives as a hang-tag ticket, printed up from behind its tear, with a warm mirror light drifting behind it and the stub floodlit from its corner: Totale, then Budget → Restano. That is Olanda's floodlit ticket, warmed from stadium green to cognac. The ticket is the only surface that carries light, so the light keeps meaning "this is your outfit".

Density is relaxed. A 760px reading column, generous gaps between turns, and one family (Inter) doing all the work through weight: black for the figures that matter, bold for titles, semibold for controls, regular for reading. Dark is the default theme. Light is a sand ground with white cards lifted by a soft shadow. Italian is the default language and English is a switch, so every string must survive the longer of the two.
keyCharacteristics: Dark espresso by default, with a sand-and-white light theme on the same tokens.
One cognac accent, used for the primary action, focus, selection and what's left of the budget.
Green, amber and red carry meaning only: in stock or success, over budget, sold out or danger.
One lit surface: the outfit ticket, with its tear, stub and mirror light.
Inter only, self-hosted and shared with olanda_project; tabular numerals for every price.
Palestra's corners: 22px cards, 14px buttons, 11px fields, 10px chips.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Cognac is the only accent. A screen has one filled cognac action; everything else is raised, ghost or chip.

rules.name: The Meaning Only Rule
rules.body: Green means in stock or success, amber means over budget, red means sold out or danger. What's left of the budget is cognac, not green, because it is the outfit's figure, not a status.

rules.name: The Variable Rule
rules.body: Colours live as per-theme variables in `index.css` and nowhere else. A new colour is a new variable in both themes.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every price, total, budget and remainder uses tabular numerals (`.tabular`).

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Buttons, chips, labels and headings are sentence case. Capitals belong to stamps and language codes, where they read as a printed tag.

rules.name: The Wordmark Rule
rules.body: "Progetto" solid and "Stile" in the cognac gradient (800, tracking −0.03em). It is the only gradient text in the app.

rules.name: The One Lit Surface Rule
rules.body: The mirror light (`.ps-glow`, the stub glow) appears only on the outfit ticket and its landing demo. Working surfaces stay unlit so the light keeps meaning "your outfit".

rules.name: The Tone Not Shadow Rule
rules.body: In the dark theme, separate surfaces by tone and hairline. Card shadows are a light-theme device.

dos: Do take every colour from the per-theme variables, and add any new colour to both themes.
Do keep one filled cognac action per screen; everything else is raised, ghost or chip.
Do set every price, total and remainder in tabular numerals, with the ticket total at 900.
Do draw every outfit as the Ticket: pieces, tear, stub reading Totale · Budget → Restano.
Do show Restano in cognac, and switch it to amber with "Oltre il budget" when the outfit goes over.
Do keep information text at Taupe Faint or stronger and at 11px or larger, and text fields at 16px.
Do write strings in Italian first and check the English switch fits the same space.
Do give every animation a reduced-motion fallback.
donts: Don't use green, amber or red for anything but in stock or success, over budget, and sold out or danger.
Don't put the mirror light, drifting orbs or a glow on any surface other than the outfit ticket.
Don't set gradient text anywhere but the "Stile" half of the wordmark.
Don't fire a success toast when outfits arrive; toasts are for errors and side effects, bottom-centre above the composer.
Don't add a second typeface. Inter is shared with olanda_project on purpose.
Don't add card shadows in the dark theme; separate by tone and hairline.
Don't use capitals outside status stamps and language codes.
